question: On the already derived p>0, R=3p^2-2P^2>0 component of the closed-FRW V=0 constraint surface, do the scalar clock phi and the geometric trace-momentum clock P define mutually consistent classical complete observables on their common chart, and where does the log-scale clock Q fail?

upstream_results.role: fixes the U_plus classical constraint component and the on-shell invariant Phi used here; it supplies no two-clock comparison or quantum clock map

primary_sources.source: B. Dittrich, Partial and Complete Observables for Canonical General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0507106
primary_sources.used_for: the classical partial/complete-observable framework and the requirement to state a clock chart
primary_sources.not_used_for: deriving the repository-specific closed-FRW invariant or proving a quantum clock equivalence

primary_sources.source: P. A. Hoehn and A. Vanrietvelde, How to switch between relational quantum clocks, arXiv:1810.04153
primary_sources.used_for: the scope warning that clock changes require a clock-neutral constrained description and careful treatment of degenerate clock regions
primary_sources.not_used_for: claiming that this classical calculation constructs their quantum reduction maps

declared_model.clock_one: scalar phi, with FP_phi={phi,C}>0 on the declared component
declared_model.clock_two: geometric trace momentum P, with FP_P={P,C}=-C_Q>0 on shell
declared_model.failed_control_clock: Q=2 log(a), whose FP factor {Q,C}=C_P vanishes at P=0 and changes sign

tasks: verify the constraint-shell identity and the weak Dirac property of Phi
derive and sign-check the phi-clock and P-clock Faddeev-Popov factors
construct P_phi(tau), Q_phi(tau), phi_P(sigma), and Q_P(sigma) from Phi and p
verify clock reading recovery, weak gauge invariance, and mutual composition on the overlap
record the finite P-clock interval, the full scalar-clock range, and the Q-clock turning-point obstruction
leave quantum clock maps, physical inner products, V-nonzero evolution, BO, decoherence, likelihood, physics and TOE outputs null

decision_table.condition: all exact constraint, Dirac, FP, complete-observable, overlap and clock-domain checks pass
decision_table.meaning: the declared classical complete observables agree where both clocks are valid; no quantum equivalence follows

decision_table.condition: any exact identity or declared clock-domain check fails
decision_table.meaning: reject this declared comparison without drawing a conclusion about other clocks or models
